summary:
Sentinel Ember is an interactive early-warning platform that monitors and analyzes wildfires across Colombia using historical and near real-time data (2025–2026). A comprehensive web dashboard featuring an Alert Intelligence center, Historical Records, and an Emergency Response module. Users can seamlessly toggle map layers between raw MODIS data, raw VIIRS data, and our physics-based harmonized view.

We built a geospatial algorithm that physically merges MODIS and VIIRS footprints using topological clustering and two-stage energy integration. This eliminates multi-sensor double-counting and calculates true radiative flux density (MW/km²). The system automatically filters alerts by severity and integrates an emergency workflow to dispatch cross-validated "Critical" events directly to local environmental authorities (IDEAM) via email.

Relying on single sensors or raw overlays creates spatial biases and false alarms. By transforming fragmented satellite telemetry into a unified, high-precision metric, Sentinel Ember provides first responders with reliable, actionable intelligence to coordinate rapid field interventions and protect vulnerable ecosystems.
details:
Sentinel Ember is a comprehensive wildfire early-warning and historical analysis engine tailored for Colombia. It ingests both Standard Processing (SP) and Near Real-Time (NRT) orbital telemetry from the NASA FIRMS API, specifically leveraging the MODIS (Terra/Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP/NOAA-20) sensor constellations. Rather than plotting raw database coordinates, it operates via a physics-based spatial harmonization algorithm. It models the true physical footprint of each satellite pixel on a metric grid accounting for orbital altitude and off-nadir bow-tie distortion and uses topological clustering to merge overlapping detections into unified fire events. The system then executes a two-stage energy integration to calculate a consolidated Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and true radiative flux density (MW/km²), automatically classifying events into Critical, Moderate, or Watch alert levels.

The primary benefit of Sentinel Ember is the elimination of multi-sensor double-counting and the correction of spatial biases caused by differing sensor resolutions (1 km vs. 375 m). Traditional platforms often duplicate fires or dilute thermal energy readings; this system provides a normalized, mathematically rigorous metric for true fire severity.

The intended impact is to equip Colombian environmental authorities (specifically IDEAM) and local dispatchers with actionable, high-fidelity intelligence. Through the integrated Emergency Response module, cross-validated "Critical" alerts can be automatically dispatched to field teams, reducing response times and protecting highly vulnerable ecosystems in the Andes and the Orinoquía. Additionally, the harmonized data allows climate researchers to study continuous historical fire calendars without the artificial data spikes typically introduced when combining legacy and modern satellite sensors.

The platform was engineered using a high-performance, open-source technical stack:

Backend & Geospatial Engine: Python serves as the core language, utilizing Pandas, GeoPandas, and PyArrow (Parquet) for rapid data processing and projection handling (reprojecting geodetic coordinates to the official EPSG:9377 MAGNA-SIRGAS metric system). Shapely powers the complex unary_union topological footprint intersections.

Visualization & Frontend: Plotly 6.0+ generates the interactive, multi-layer web mapping (allowing toggles between raw and harmonized data), while Matplotlib handles static, publication-ready exports. The full Command Center dashboard featuring Alert Intelligence, Historical Records, and Emergency Response routing is built and deployed via Streamlit

APIs & Data Sources: The NASA FIRMS API provides the active fire telemetry, while GADM datasets are used for Level-1 departmental spatial clipping.

Development Environment: The development of Sentinel Ember was engineered on Windows environments using Lenovo LOQ 15IAX9E and Pavilion 0014LA hardware via Visual Studio Code 1.46.0, leveraging a high-performance hybrid architecture. The geospatial core, written in Python 3.15.1, uses requests to ingest NASA FIRMS API data (MODIS and VIIRS), alongside pandas, numpy, geopandas, and shapely for data processing, spatial clipping to Colombia, and physical footprint clustering, generating visualizations with Plotly Express. This pipeline feeds a lightweight backend built in TypeScript 7.0 using the Hono 4.13 HTTP framework on Node.js (tsx 4.23). The dashboard frontend was developed in React 19.3 and bundled with Vite 8.3, seamlessly integrating native interactive maps via Leaflet 1.9 and embedded Plotly HTML iframes, while streamlining the development workflow with oxlint and concurrently for a final agile deployment on Vercel.

The core creativity of Sentinel Ember lies in treating satellite telemetry as a strict applied physics and radiometry problem, rather than a basic software mapping task. By modeling the physics of the sensors, the algorithm weights the coordinates of merged centroids inversely proportional to the square of the pixel area (wi ∝ Ai-2). This creatively anchors the unified location to the highly precise VIIRS sensor while preserving the robust energy validation of MODIS. During development, several critical operational and environmental factors were considered. The team accounted for heavy atmospheric interference and convective cloud cover in tropical regions, which necessitates combining multiple satellite passes to secure a clear thermal reading. Furthermore, we considered the exact workflow of emergency responders; this drove the decision to evolve the project from a simple analytical map into a complete incident lifecycle manager, bridging the gap between raw orbital data and on-the-ground dispatch coordination.
